facts.analysis: Brissett threw the ball nearly 50 times in his first game with the Ravens. He was able to rack up 340 yards in the process, but he didn't score any touchdowns, which left him with an underwhelming fantasy score individually. He was able to successfully support Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews, but the team will almost certainly want him to throw significantly less passes on a game-to-game basis moving forward, so those guys may not have the consistent workload that this week suggested they might.

facts.analysis: Brissett looked like a natural fit in coordinator Declan Doyle's offense despite having only practiced a handful of days with the Ravens following his trade from the Cardinals, amassing his highest passing yardage total since Week 11 of last season. As he'd often done with Trey McBride in Arizona, Brissett focused heavily on the tight-end position in his Baltimore debut, connecting with Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas a combined 11 times for 119 yards. Brissett recorded completions to seven different targets overall, but his one interception did lead to a Chargers touchdown. Brissett's prospects in this offense look bright if his first game is any indication, and he'll look to carry over the momentum into a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday.

facts.report: Jacoby Brissett a Strong Superflex Start in Ravens Debut: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett will debut with his new team on Monday in Week 10 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett was benched by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8 and subsequently traded to the Ravens, who desperately needed a quarterback after placing Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve. Jackson still has a chance to return this season, but Brissett will lead the offense for the time being, putting him in charge of keeping the team's playoff hopes alive. The veteran quarterback flashed upside at times in Arizona, but he finished the first half of the season with a discouraging 11-to-7 touchdown-to-turnover ratio. His days of being a potential fantasy QB1 are over, but he can still be a top-24 or perhaps even a top-18 option, giving him legitimate appeal in plenty of superflex and 2-QB leagues. He should also benefit from having a strong supporting cast at his disposal, including wide receiver Zay Flowers and tight end Mark Andrews. This week, Brissett ranks as RotoBaller's QB19 as he takes on a Chargers defense that ranks near the middle of the league with 13 passing touchdowns and seven interceptions allowed.

facts.report: Elic Ayomanor Drawing Interest After Increased Workload: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Elic Ayomanor caught five passes for 79 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to Jacksonville. He was targeted 10 times, setting season highs in all three categories. With Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined, Ayomanor played nearly 95% of Tennessee's offensive snaps and led the team in receiving. Wan'Dale Robinson also left Sunday's game with an ankle injury, leaving the Titans potentially short-handed at receiver heading into Week 11 against Dallas. Ayomanor saw just five targets in his previous game against Cincinnati, so Sunday's workload was a big jump. He's worth a look in 12-team leagues and deeper, particularly if Tate or Robinson misses additional time.

facts.report: Seth McGowan Is a Week 11 Bench Stash: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan carried the ball on 12 of his 17 offensive snaps against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. He finished with 77 yards and a touchdown after rushing for 45 yards and a score on six carries against the Dallas Cowboys. His snap share slipped from 31% to 29% across those games. Before Sunday, he'd reached double-digit carries just once, with 11 against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. Both touchdowns came from inside the five-yard line, giving McGowan some flex appeal in 14-team half-PPR leagues on Thursday at Houston. McGowan has five catches for nine yards all season, and Jonathan Taylor drew all four backfield targets against Miami. Taylor also led Indianapolis with 16 carries and played 40 offensive snaps. Rostered in 18% of Yahoo leagues, McGowan is worth a bench spot in 12-team half-PPR leagues, especially for Taylor managers. McGowan handled every other running back touch against Miami, and DJ Giddens played just two offensive snaps. That split puts McGowan first in line for more carries if Taylor misses time.

evidence.scoringBasis: news from the past week

facts.analysis: The rookie had shown well in recent weeks while trade speculation swirled around Jonathan Taylor, and even though the latter ultimately stayed put at the deadline, McGowan still compiled a new career high in rush attempts and rushing yards. The Kentucky product also followed up his first career rushing touchdown in Week 9 against the Cowboys with a four-yard scoring run early in the second quarter Sunday, and McGowan was also productive in his returner role. While Taylor should remain the de facto top backfield option for the Colts, McGowan should remain in an elevated role for what remains of Indianapolis' non-contending season.
facts.report: Seth McGowan - Retains expanded role Sunday: McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 61 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
